exports.name: ColumnAlign
exports.description:

exports.name: ColumnPin
exports.description:
The edge a column is pinned to. `start` and `end` follow the reading direction (the inline start and end, as MUI X's
pinned columns do under right to left); `left` and `right` keep their physical meaning. `left` / `start` columns are
drawn first, `right` / `end` columns last.

exports.name: DataGridAdapter
exports.description:
Headless data layer. The grid is fully driven by an adapter — swap any
backend (REST / GraphQL / Linear / Prisma / in-memory) by implementing
this interface. Mutators are optional; when omitted, the matching
affordances hide automatically.

The `TWhere` generic mirrors the backend's filter input shape — fields'
`toWhere` callbacks merge into a single `TWhere` that `load()` receives.

exports.description: Which optional features an adapter supports, read from the methods and config it provides.

exports.name: MaybePromise

exports.description: Reads an adapter's capabilities from the methods and config it provides; pagination is cursor-only unless the adapter declares otherwise.

exports.name: createInMemoryAdapter

Reference adapter — applies search / filters / sort / pagination over a
plain array. Use as a stand-in for prototyping or as a pattern reference
when wiring a real backend.

exports.name: dayBounds
exports.description:
A stored single-date value → the whole local day it names, for the date
operator `eq` ("is"): "on this calendar day", not "at this instant". Uses
the same local time zone as the date control, so the day the user clicked
is the day that matches. The end is the day's last millisecond, inclusive,
matching the date-range presets. Null when empty or unparseable.

exports.name: DayBounds
exports.description: The inclusive start and end of one calendar day, as ISO timestamps.

exports.name: InMemoryAdapterOptions

exports.name: InMemoryAdapter
exports.description:
In-memory adapter — public shape. The base `DataGridAdapter` plus a
`push` / `remove` hatch so demos + tests can drive realtime upserts
without standing up a fake WebSocket. Real adapters connect to their
own push source inside `subscribe()`.

props.name: adapter
props.description: Where the grid's rows come from: its loader, filter and search config, capabilities and mutators.

props.name: optimistic
props.description:
Apply mutations locally before the adapter resolves so the UI feels
instant. Rolls back on error.

Affects: `updateRow`, `deleteRow`, `bulkUpdate`, `bulkDelete`. Skipped
for `duplicateRow / moveRow / bulkMoveRows` (those need the server
to compute the new id / position).

props.name: paginationMode
props.description:
- `paged` (default): each filter/sort/cursor change replaces `rows`.
  Drives `<DataGridPagination>` (prev/next + page-size). Cursor-based
  adapter contract (`first / after / last / before`).
- `infinite`: filter/sort change resets to first page; `loadMore('down')`
  appends the next page (forward cursor) and `loadMore('up')` prepends
  the previous page (backward cursor). Cursor-based.
- `numbered`: classic offset/limit pagination — supports jump-to-page-N.
  Drives `<DataGridNumberedPagination>` (1 2 3 … N) and friends.
  Adapter must declare `pagination: { offset: true }` or the provider
  raises a clear error at mount.

The same accumulated `rows` array drives every layout (table / cards /
kanban / media-grid / virt) — no per-layout duplication.

props.name: history
props.description:
Undo and redo of edits (inline edit, paste, bulk edit) with Mod+Z / Mod+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y inside the grid
and `DataGridUndoRedo`. On by default whenever the adapter has `updateRow`, keeping
`DATAGRID_HISTORY_LIMIT` (100) steps; `{ limit }` changes that, `false` turns it off. A new adapter or a
`refresh()` clears it.

props.description: The grid and its toolbar parts, which read the loaded data through `useDataGrid()`.

exports.name: dispatchRowMove
exports.description:
Standard adapter dispatch helper — picks the best mutator for the
move based on what the adapter implements. Use in your `onMove`
callback when you don't need anything custom.

  const dispatch = useDispatchRowMove(useDataGrid())
  // ...
  onMove: (ids, beforeId) => dispatch(ids, beforeId),

Priority: `bulkMoveRows(ids, beforeId)` > N × `moveRow(id, beforeId)`.
No-op if neither mutator is available.
